
::: {.cs-note}
Fall FTE students (full-time plus part-time converted with the NCES Digest part-time factors, as in Delta Cost), surviving sets: S24 for the index (1,909 institutions), S11 for the share that shrank (2,038). Peer groups: **flagships** are each state's flagship campus with its own branches (42 states; 8 states whose flagship sits inside a system-wide unit are excluded); **regional publics** are public master's and bachelor's colleges other than flagships; **small privates** are private bachelor's colleges with fewer than 2,000 FTE students in FY2012. Survivor sets exclude colleges that closed, which were mostly small and shrinking, so declines are understated. FY2024–25 NCES provisional.
:::

## Staff or students? Decomposing the rise in staff per student

The change in staff per student is the change in staff minus the change in students (in log points, about percent). Bars to the right of zero raise staff per student; a falling enrollment bar (the denominator) raises it too. The default shows faculty FTE and non-faculty FTE side by side (full-time + one-third of part-time; faculty excludes graduate assistants). The denominator is the same for every staff measure.

{{< include ../_toggles.qmd >}}

```{ojs}
viewof by = Inputs.select(new Map([["All institutions", "all"], ["Sector", "sector"], ["Enrollment-growth third (within sector)", "third"], ["Enrollment rose or fell", "rosefell"], ["Peer group", "peer"], ["Online enrollment rose or fell", "online"]]), {value: param("by", "sector"), label: "Group by"})
viewof ver = Inputs.select(new Map([["Total FTE, FY2013–24 (headline)", "b"], ["On-campus FTE only, FY2013–24", "c"], ["Total FTE, FY2012–24 (continuous categories only)", "a"]]), {value: param("v", "b"), label: "Students"})
DMK = ["pair", ...MEAS.map(d => d.k).filter(k => k !== "pair" && DE.some(d => d.measure === k))]
viewof dm = measSelect(DMK, {value: param("dm", "pair"), label: "Staff"})
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
DMS = dm === "pair" ? PAIR : [dm]
// FY2012–24 window only for measures with no part-time faculty or GAs (same rule as faculty FTE)
VERA = new Set(["nonfacfte", "ftfac"])
DML = k => dm === "pair" ? PAIRL[k] : "Staff"
```

```{ojs}
{
  setParam("by", by === "sector" ? null : by); setParam("v", ver === "b" ? null : ver); setParam("dm", dm === "pair" ? null : dm);
  const p = wt === "w" ? "w" : "u";
  const rows = DE.filter(d => d.grouping === by && d.ver === ver && DMS.includes(d.measure));
  if (!rows.length || (ver === "a" && DMS.some(m => !VERA.has(m) || !rows.some(r => r.measure === m)))) return md`*No FY2012–24 decomposition for this measure: it is not comparable across the 2012–13 HR redesign (it contains part-time faculty or graduate assistants, which are spliced there, or executive, professional and nonprofessional staff, which were reclassified). Choose FY2013–24.*`;
  const groups = [...new Set(rows.map(d => d.group))];
  const order = by === "sector" ? SECTORS.map(s => s.l).filter(l => groups.includes(l)) : groups;
  const COMP = [...DMS.map(m => `${DML(m)}`), "Students (denominator)", ...DMS.map(m => `${DML(m)} per student`)];
  const CC = dm === "pair" ? [LIGHT, "#f2c18d", GRAY, BLUE, "#c8701e"] : [LIGHT, GRAY, BLUE];
  const long = order.flatMap(g => {
    const rr = DMS.map(m => rows.find(d => d.group === g && d.measure === m)).filter(Boolean);
    if (!rr.length) return [];
    return [...rr.map(d => ({g, c: DML(d.measure), v: d[`${p}_staff`], d})), {g, c: "Students (denominator)", v: rr[0][`${p}_den`], d: rr[0]}, ...rr.map(d => ({g, c: `${DML(d.measure)} per student`, v: d[`${p}_ratio`], d}))];
  }).map(x => ({...x, n: x.d.n, a: x.d[`${p}aa`], b: x.d[`${p}ab`], m: x.d.measure}));
  const narrow = width < 640;
  return html`${Plot.plot({
    width: Math.min(width, 900), height: 50 + order.length * (dm === "pair" ? 100 : 66), marginLeft: narrow ? 110 : 210, marginRight: 50,
    x: {grid: true, insetLeft: 36, insetRight: 36, label: `Log points ×100, ${rows[0].window.replace("FY2013-FY2024", "FY2013–24").replace("FY2012-FY2024", "FY2012–24")} (${wlab})`},
    y: {domain: COMP, axis: null}, fy: {domain: order, label: null},
    color: {domain: COMP, range: CC, legend: true},
    marks: [Plot.ruleX([0], {stroke: INK}),
      Plot.barX(long, {fy: "g", y: "c", x: "v", fill: "c", inset: 1}),
      Plot.text(long.filter(d => d.v < 0), {fy: "g", y: "c", x: "v", text: d => s1(d.v), dx: -4, textAnchor: "end", fontSize: 10, fill: INK}),
      Plot.text(long.filter(d => d.v >= 0), {fy: "g", y: "c", x: "v", text: d => s1(d.v), dx: 4, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 10, fill: INK}),
      Plot.tip(long, Plot.pointerY({fy: "g", y: "c", x: "v", title: d => `${d.g}: ${d.c} ${s1(d.v)}\n${MEASL[d.m]} per 1,000: ${f1(d.a)} → ${f1(d.b)}\n${d.n} institutions`}))]
  })}
  <div class="cs-scroll"><table class="cs-sectab"><thead><tr><th>Group</th>${dm === "pair" ? html`<th>Measure</th>` : ""}<th>n</th><th>Per 1,000, start</th><th>Per 1,000, FY2024</th><th>Staff</th><th>Students</th><th>Staff per student</th></tr></thead><tbody>
  ${order.flatMap(g => DMS.map(m => { const d = rows.find(r => r.group === g && r.measure === m); return d ? html`<tr><td>${g}</td>${dm === "pair" ? html`<td>${PAIRL[m]}</td>` : ""}<td>${d.n}</td><td>${f1(d[`${p}aa`])}</td><td>${f1(d[`${p}ab`])}</td><td>${s1(d[`${p}_staff`])}</td><td>${s1(d[`${p}_den`])}</td><td><b>${s1(d[`${p}_ratio`])}</b></td></tr>` : ""; }))}
  </tbody></table></div>${dm === "ga" ? html`<p class="cs-note">Graduate assistants: research sectors only; small n.</p>` : ""}`;
}
```

::: {.cs-note}
S11 surviving set (2,038 institutions). Unweighted: means of institution log changes, so the identity holds exactly for the typical institution. Weighted: log changes of group totals. On-campus FTE removes students enrolled exclusively online (IPEDS distance-education counts), so it shows staff per student actually on campus. Growth thirds are formed within each sector on FY2012–24 FTE change. The FY2012–24 version is the earlier (item 10) window; it is shown only for measures that contain no part-time faculty or graduate assistants and are continuous across the 2012–13 HR redesign (non-faculty FTE and full-time faculty), not for faculty FTE, all FTE excluding graduate assistants, v1 FTE staff, part-time faculty, graduate assistants, the v1 headcounts or executive, professional and nonprofessional staff, all of which contain part-time faculty spliced at the redesign or were reclassified there. At community colleges non-faculty FTE also steps up about 1 log point (part-time staff) at the redesign, so use FY2013–24 there. FY2024 NCES provisional.
:::

::: {.cs-note}
Exclusively online students as a share of fall headcount, S24 set. Falls 2020–21 (shaded, FY2021–22) are distorted by COVID; FY2025 is NCES provisional. Counting only on-campus students more than doubles the rise in staff per student for every staff measure (faculty FTE and non-faculty FTE alike; the staff measure on this chart follows the "Staff" choice above): online growth offset about half of the fall in on-campus enrollment.
:::

## Dual enrollment

High-school students taking college courses are counted as college enrollment. Their growth hides part of the community-college decline. IPEDS has no dual-enrollment item, so the proxy is undergraduates under 18, converted to FTE.

<div class="cs-two">

Sector groups pool public master's and bachelor's colleges (regional publics) and private master's and bachelor's colleges. FY2014–24 changes use the S11 set, unweighted. No measurable spillover from state dual-enrollment growth to four-year enrollment was found. FY2024 NCES provisional.
:::
